new.title: Trace 130 years of the car at the Mercedes-Benz Museum
new.desc: A spiral of nine levels tells the story of the automobile from Daimler and Benz's 1886 inventions to modern concept cars, in a UNStudio building opened in 2006. The collection holds around 160 vehicles.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 to 18:00, closed Mondays; last ticket at 17:00. Take S-Bahn S1 to Neckarpark.
new.q: Mercedes-Benz Museum, Mercedesstraße 100, Bad Cannstatt, Stuttgart

new.title: Admire the racing legends at the Porsche Museum
new.desc: The 2009 Delugan Meissl building at Porscheplatz presents about 80 vehicles, from the 1948 Porsche 356 No. 1 to Le Mans winners. It sits beside the Zuffenhausen factory.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 9:00 to 18:00, closed Mondays; shut 18 January to 1 February 2027 for refurbishment. S-Bahn S6 to Neuwirtshaus.

new.title: See Picasso and Stirling's postmodern icon at the Staatsgalerie
new.desc: The Neue Staatsgalerie by James Stirling opened in 1984 and is a landmark of postmodern architecture. It shows works by Picasso, Beckmann and Schlemmer, whose Triadic Ballet figures are a highlight.
new.tip: Open most days to 17:00, with late opening on Thursday until 20:00. The ramp around the central rotunda is open to the public.

new.title: Walk through Württemberg history in the Altes Schloss
new.desc: The Landesmuseum Württemberg occupies the Renaissance Old Castle, the former residence of the counts and dukes. Collections include the Celtic Hochdorf finds, the Crown Jewels of Württemberg and a Kunstkammer.
new.tip: Check current hours and prices on the museum site. The arcaded courtyard is free to enter.
new.q: Landesmuseum Württemberg, Altes Schloss, Schillerplatz 6, Stuttgart-Mitte

new.title: Discover world cultures at the Linden-Museum
new.desc: One of Germany's major ethnological museums, founded in 1884, with collections from Africa, Asia, the Americas and Oceania. It has been working on the colonial provenance of its holdings.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 17:00 and Sunday to 18:00, closed Mondays. A short walk from the Hauptbahnhof.

new.title: Learn the city's story at the StadtPalais
new.desc: The Museum für Stuttgart in the former Palais Gutbrod tells the city's history from the earliest settlement to the present. The permanent exhibition has free admission.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00 with Fridays until 21:00. There is a café on the ground floor.
new.q: StadtPalais - Museum für Stuttgart, Konrad-Adenauer-Straße 2, Stuttgart-Mitte

new.title: Follow the history of Baden-Württemberg at the Haus der Geschichte
new.desc: A museum by the Staatsgalerie covering the history of the state since 1800 with objects, media stations and everyday items, including the founding of the state in 1952.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; check current hours on the official site. Combine with the Staatsgalerie next door.
new.q: Haus der Geschichte Baden-Württemberg, Konrad-Adenauer-Straße 16, Stuttgart-Mitte

new.title: Walk the Weissenhof Estate of 1927
new.desc: The Weissenhofsiedlung was built for the 1927 Werkbund exhibition with houses by Mies van der Rohe, Le Corbusier, Walter Gropius and others. Two Le Corbusier buildings belong to the UNESCO World Heritage series of his work.
new.tip: The Weissenhofmuseum in the Le Corbusier house is open Tuesday to Sunday, 11:00 to 18:00. The estate is a residential area, so stay on the paths.

new.title: Ride up the world's first concrete TV tower
new.desc: The Stuttgart TV Tower in Degerloch, finished in 1956 and designed by Fritz Leonhardt, was the first telecommunications tower built of reinforced concrete and inspired many later towers. Its platform looks over the city and vineyards.
new.tip: Book timed tickets online in summer. Go before sunset on a clear day.

new.title: Admire the Neues Schloss on Schlossplatz
new.desc: The Baroque New Palace, built from 1746 to 1807 for the Dukes and later Kings of Württemberg, is one of the largest in the region. After war damage it was rebuilt and now houses ministries.
new.tip: Walk around the Schlossplatz with its Jubilee Column and the park behind. The interior is mostly closed.

new.title: Visit the Stiftskirche above Schillerplatz
new.desc: The Collegiate Church is the main Protestant church of the city with a Gothic core, and its two uneven towers are a city landmark. It was rebuilt after wartime destruction.
new.tip: Entry is free and concerts are held regularly. Combine with the nearby Markthalle.

new.title: Study Bonatz's Hauptbahnhof tower and station hall
new.desc: Paul Bonatz and Friedrich Eugen Scholer designed the main station, built from 1914 to 1927, whose 56 m tower carries a Mercedes star. The new underground station of Stuttgart 21 lies below it.
new.tip: The old hall is free to enter.

new.title: Climb to the Württemberg Mausoleum on Rotenberg
new.desc: King Wilhelm I of Württemberg had the Grabkapelle built in 1820 to 1824 for his wife Katharina, on the site of the ancestral castle. A Greek-inspired rotunda, it stands among vineyards with long views over the Neckar valley.
new.tip: A small fee is charged to enter; check the opening days. Take bus 61 or walk up from Rotenberg village.
new.q: Grabkapelle auf dem Württemberg, Württembergstraße, Rotenberg, Stuttgart

new.title: Spend a day at the Wilhelma zoo and botanical garden
new.desc: The Wilhelma is a Moorish-style royal garden of the 1840s that is today a combined zoo and botanical garden with around 1,000 animal species. Its magnolia grove and historic greenhouses are as famous as the animals.
new.tip: Arrive at opening and avoid summer weekends. Check Wilhelma's site for the ticket price.

new.title: Stand on Monte Scherbelino, the rubble mountain
new.desc: The Birkenkopf is a 511 m hill raised partly from wartime rubble cleared from the city after 1945. A summit cross, a memorial and views of the basin crown it.
new.tip: Free and always open; trails are rocky, so wear good shoes. Go in late afternoon.

new.title: See the city from Eugensplatz and the Eugenstaffel
new.desc: Eugensplatz with its Galatea fountain is a terrace on the slope of the basin with a classic panorama over the centre. The Eugenstaffel stairs lead down toward the city.
new.tip: Reached by tram U15 to Eugensplatz. Evening light is best.

new.title: Catch the view at Haigst and Santiago-de-Chile-Platz
new.desc: A terraced viewpoint above Marienplatz with an orientation board naming the sights over Schlossplatz and the basin. It is less known than Karlshöhe and Eugensplatz.
new.tip: A short walk from the Zacke's Haigst stop. Bring a picnic.

new.title: Stroll the Höhenpark Killesberg and its tower
new.desc: A garden show park laid out on a former quarry in 1939 and expanded for the 1993 garden exhibition, with a rose garden, a lookout tower and a narrow-gauge railway.
new.tip: Free to enter outside special events. Take U7 or U5 to Killesberg.

new.title: Meet the fossils at Museum Schloss Rosenstein
new.desc: The neoclassical Rosenstein Palace of 1824 to 1830 houses one branch of the Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde with fossils, minerals and large mammal exhibits, set in Rosensteinpark.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; check the official site for prices. Walk to it through Rosensteinpark from the Wilhelma.
new.q: Museum Schloss Rosenstein, Rosenstein 1, Bad Cannstatt, Stuttgart

new.title: Look at the cube-shaped Stadtbibliothek
new.desc: The city library of 2011 by Eun Young Yi is a white cube with a glass-block facade that glows at night and an atrium of stacked galleries. It is a modern landmark near the Hauptbahnhof.
new.tip: Free to enter; the reading hall and roof terrace are open during library hours.

new.title: Climb the Stäffele to Karlshöhe for a wide view
new.desc: The 344 m hill, once a quarry and called Reinsburghügel, has a green terrace with a panorama over the south and west of the city. It is a stop on several Stäffele routes.
new.tip: A beer garden operates here in summer. Reach it via the Willy-Reichert-Staffel from Marienplatz.

new.title: Wander the lanes of the Bohnenviertel
new.desc: The Bohnenviertel is Stuttgart's old craftsmen's quarter, where small old houses survived near the Leonhardskirche. It is lively with wine rooms and a neighbourhood festival.
new.tip: Walk Wagnerstraße and the streets nearby in the evening.

new.title: Eat Maultaschen in the courtyard of Weinstube Fröhlich
new.desc: A casual Swabian wine bar with a woody interior serving homemade Maultaschen, Zwiebelrostbraten, Spätzle and potato salad, with an inner courtyard for summer.
new.tip: Order Maultaschen, in broth or pan-fried with egg. Reserve for dinner.

new.title: Order Zwiebelrostbraten at Weinhaus Stetter
new.desc: A long-established wine shop and Weinstube in the Leonhardsviertel, listed by Stuttgart's tourism board for Swabian cooking. Its Zwiebelrostbraten is the dish pictured in the official food guide.
new.tip: Go for lunch or dinner and choose a Württemberg red such as Trollinger or Lemberger.

new.title: Dine in the 1564 Schellenturm city-wall tower
new.desc: Weinstube Schellenturm is set in a tower of the old city wall at Weberstraße, dated to 1564, and serves Maultaschen and Spätzle in vaulted rooms.
new.tip: Reserve in the evening and ask for a seat inside the tower.

new.title: Share a bottle at Weinstube Zur Kiste
new.desc: Zur Kiste claims to be one of Stuttgart's oldest Weinstuben and serves Swabian dishes in a traditional room near the Bohnenviertel.
new.tip: Open in the evening, around 17:00 to 23:00; reserve ahead.

new.title: Eat Swabian classics at the Alte Kanzlei
new.desc: The Alte Kanzlei in a 16th-century chancellery building on Schillerplatz serves Maultaschen, Zwiebelrostbraten and Flädlesuppe, with a terrace facing the Stiftskirche.
new.tip: Open daily from morning; the terrace in summer is good for coffee and cake.

new.title: Try dry-aged Zwiebelrostbraten at Zur Weinsteige
new.desc: A traditional restaurant run by Andreas Scherle on the Weinsteige, known for hearty Swabian vespers and a dry-aged Zwiebelrostbraten.
new.tip: Reserve for dinner; the garden is pleasant in summer.

new.title: Graze through the Art Nouveau Markthalle
new.desc: The Markthalle of 1914 is a covered market in Jugendstil style with produce, cheese, wine and ready meals. Swabian bakers, butchers and food stalls sit alongside international stalls.
new.tip: Open Monday to Friday from about 7:30 and Saturdays until about 17:00. Buy a pretzel and sausage, then eat in the gallery.

new.title: Drink beer at Tschechen & Söhne on Karlshöhe
new.desc: A beer garden on top of Karlshöhe with views of the basin, known as a popular meeting point on the hill.
new.tip: Best on summer evenings. Climb the Stäffele to earn your drink.

new.title: Have tea at the Teehaus in Weißenburgpark
new.desc: A pavilion on the Weißenburgpark terrace above the south of the city, with a beer garden in good weather and a viewing terrace a short walk away.
new.tip: Open April to October, except in rain or cold.

new.title: Drink Trollinger at Zieglers Besen in Uhlbach
new.desc: A Besenwirtschaft in Uhlbach serving typical Swabian dishes with its own wines, open for set weeks. The 2026 schedule listed 15 to 21 March, 12 to 18 April and 17 to 23 May, plus a week in November.
new.tip: Check dates before going, as the weeks change each year.

new.title: Taste at the Sonnen-Besen Zaiß in Obertürkheim
new.desc: The Besenwirtschaft of the Zaiß family at Uhlbacher Straße 23 opens in winter and autumn. A 2026 listing shows it open until 29 March, and a 2025 autumn season ran from 17 October to 30 November.
new.tip: Open daily from 11:00, closed Mondays in season. Try the sausage salad and a Württemberg red.
new.q: Sonnen-Besen Zaiß, Uhlbacher Straße 23, Obertürkheim, Stuttgart

new.title: Eat among the vines at Besenwirtschaft Gerhard Zaiß
new.desc: A Besenwirtschaft in the Gehrenwald vineyards near Rotenberg, usually open in May and from mid-August to mid-September.
new.tip: Open only in season; check the dates and carry cash.
new.q: Besenwirtschaft Gerhard Zaiß, Gehrenwald, Rotenberg, Stuttgart

new.title: Visit the Besen of Weingut Schwarz in Untertürkheim
new.desc: A family wine estate whose Besenwirtschaft has run since 1967, open in the autumn and winter months and for a spring week (8 to 17 April in 2025).
new.tip: Check the current season on the estate's site.

new.title: Drink at the Karl Wöhrwag Besen in Untertürkheim
new.desc: A winery's Besenwirtschaft open in September and from January to early March, serving Swabian plates beside estate wines.
new.tip: Open only during the season; check the dates first.

new.title: Dine on elevated Swabian food in the Zirbelstube
new.desc: The Zirbelstube in the Hotel Le Méridien is an elegant wood-panelled restaurant serving traditional Swabian dishes at fine-dining level.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; dress smart-casual.
new.q: Zirbelstube, Hotel Le Méridien, Willy-Brandt-Straße 30, Stuttgart-Mitte

new.title: Grab a Currywurst at Tobi's on Königstraße
new.desc: A Swabian-focused street food stand on Königstraße, listed in Falstaff's street food guide for its currywurst.
new.tip: Cheap and quick, a good stop between museums.

new.title: Walk the Stäffele from Marienplatz to Karlshöhe
new.desc: Stuttgart has hundreds of public stairways, the Stäffele, climbing the slopes of the basin. A route from Marienplatz up the Else-Himmelheber-Staffel and Willy-Reichert-Staffel to Karlshöhe is around 400 steps.
new.tip: Allow one and a half to two hours and wear good shoes. Guided Stäffele tours also run.

new.title: Ride the Zacke rack railway to Degerloch
new.desc: Line U10 is a rack railway from Marienplatz up to Degerloch, a rare urban rack line that climbs the slope through villas and vineyards.
new.tip: A standard VVS ticket is valid. Ride to Haigst or Degerloch.

new.title: Soak in the mineral waters at LEUZE
new.desc: Stuttgart's springs are among the richest mineral water sources in Europe. Mineralbad Leuze is one of three municipal spas, with indoor and outdoor pools.
new.tip: Mineralbad Berg is closed until the end of 2026; LEUZE and SoleBad are open.
new.q: Mineralbad Leuze, Am Leuzebad 2-6, Bad Cannstatt, Stuttgart

new.title: Float in the SoleBad Cannstatt
new.desc: A saline thermal pool open all year, fed by Cannstatt's springs, near the Cannstatter Wasen.
new.tip: Check current opening hours before going.
new.q: SoleBad Cannstatt, Sulzerrainstraße 2, Bad Cannstatt, Stuttgart

new.title: Taste wines at the Stuttgarter Weindorf
new.desc: The Weindorf is a wine festival in the city centre on Marktplatz, Schillerplatz and Kirchstraße, where winemakers pour from small wooden huts. The 2026 edition ran from 20 August to 5 September and marked its 50th anniversary.
new.tip: Admission is free. Try Trollinger, Riesling and Lemberger.

new.title: Join the Cannstatter Volksfest on the Wasen
new.desc: One of the largest beer festivals in Germany, running about 16 days on the Cannstatter Wasen, with beer tents, rides and the Fruchtsäule. It dates back to 1818.
new.tip: It runs from late September into early October; check exact dates.

new.title: Ride the Ferris wheel at the Frühlingsfest
new.desc: The spring counterpart to the Volksfest on the Cannstatter Wasen, with beer tents, a big Ferris wheel and rides.
new.tip: Held in April and May; check dates.

new.title: Browse the Stuttgart Christmas market
new.desc: One of the largest and oldest Christmas markets in Germany, spread across the old town around Schillerplatz and Schlossplatz. The 2026 market runs from 25 November to 23 December.
new.tip: Visit on a weekday evening to avoid crowds. Try Glühwein and roasted chestnuts.

new.title: Hike the Rotenberg vineyards to the Württemberg chapel
new.desc: A walk through terraced vineyards to the Grabkapelle on Rotenberg, with views of the Neckar valley.
new.tip: Combine with a Besenwirtschaft in season. Allow about two hours.

new.title: Walk the Schlossgarten to Rosensteinpark
new.desc: A green belt of parks runs from the Neues Schloss to Rosensteinpark and the Wilhelma, about 4 km, with ponds and old trees.
new.tip: Flat and easy; good by bike.

new.title: Ride the Killesbergbahn miniature railway
new.desc: A narrow-gauge train that runs through the Höhenpark Killesberg and its rose garden.
new.tip: Runs in warm months; check the timetable.

new.title: Stroll the gardens of Hohenheim Palace
new.desc: The Exotic Garden and the palace of the University of Hohenheim in Plieningen are an 18th-century landscape with greenhouses.
new.tip: Open in the warm months; check opening days.

new.title: Catch a performance by the Stuttgart Ballet
new.desc: The Stuttgart Ballet, shaped by John Cranko from 1961, is one of the world's leading companies and performs in the Opernhaus of the Staatstheater.
new.tip: Book months ahead; cheaper standing tickets sometimes exist.

new.title: Circle the Max-Eyth-See by the Neckar
new.desc: An artificial lake of the 1930s on the Neckar in Mühlhausen, with paths around it, views of the vineyards and a few restaurants.
new.tip: A flat loop of a few kilometres; the Neckar towpath leads onwards.

new.title: Walk the Uhlbach vineyards above the Neckar
new.desc: A wine walk above Uhlbach with views across the Neckar valley, passing Besenwirtschaften in season.
new.tip: Combine with the Besen season; the September harvest is colourful.
